claim: PSD-95 MAGUK family scaffold proteins contain three PDZ domains followed by an SH3-GK domain tandem.
source: PSD-95 MAGUK family scaffold proteins are multi-domain organisers of synaptic transmission that contain three PDZ domains followed by an SH3-GK domain tandem.
evidence: This is a direct statement in the abstract describing the domain architecture of PSD-95.

claim: Binding of monomeric CRIPT-derived PDZ3 ligands to the third PDZ domain of PSD-95 induces functional changes in the intramolecular SH3-GK domain assembly.
source: Here we show that binding of monomeric CRIPT-derived PDZ3 ligands to the third PDZ domain of PSD-95 induces functional changes in the intramolecular SH3-GK domain assembly that influence subsequent homotypic and heterotypic complex formation.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: The heterotrimeric G protein subunit Gnb5 is a PSD-95 complex partner at dendritic spines of rat hippocampal neurons.
source: Among these interactors, we further establish the heterotrimeric G protein subunit Gnb5 as a PSD-95 complex partner at dendritic spines of rat hippocampal neurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 3C.

claim: The PSD-95 GK domain binds to Gnb5.
source: The PSD-95 GK domain binds to Gnb5, and this interaction is triggered by CRIPT-derived PDZ3 ligands binding to the third PDZ domain of PSD-95, unraveling a hierarchical binding mechanism of PSD-95 complex formation.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by coimmunoprecipitation and GST pull-down experiments.

claim: The Gnb5-PSD-95 interaction is triggered by CRIPT-derived PDZ3 ligands binding to the third PDZ domain of PSD-95.
source: The PSD-95 GK domain binds to Gnb5, and this interaction is triggered by CRIPT-derived PDZ3 ligands binding to the third PDZ domain of PSD-95, unraveling a hierarchical binding mechanism of PSD-95 complex formation.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by coimmunoprecipitation experiments in Figure 4.

claim: Excitatory synapses are contact sites through which neurons communicate with each other.
source: Excitatory synapses are the contact sites through which neurons communicate with each other.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about synaptic function.

claim: Incoming action potentials are converted into chemical signals (neurotransmitters) at presynaptic terminals.
source: Incoming action potentials are converted into chemical signals (neurotransmitters) at presynaptic terminals, which subsequently pass through the synaptic cleft and are reconverted into electrical signals at postsynaptic sites (Lisman et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Synaptic contacts are able to undergo structural changes and thereby modify neuronal network computation.
source: These synaptic contacts are not static but are able to undergo structural changes and thereby modify neuronal network computation (Nishiyama and Yasuda, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: At postsynaptic sites, interacting proteins are densely packed into a sub-membrane structure called the postsynaptic density (PSD).
source: At postsynaptic sites, interacting proteins are densely packed into a sub-membrane structure called the postsynaptic density (PSD) (Sheng and Hoogenraad, 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: PSD-95 family MAGUKs are highly abundant components of the PSD and function as central regulators of postsynaptic organisation.
source: Scaffold proteins of the PSD-95 family membrane-associated guanylate kinases (MAGUKs) are highly abundant components of the PSD and function as central regulators of postsynaptic organisation (Zhu et al., 2016a).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: PSD-95 family MAGUKs directly interact with NMDA receptor C-termini.
source: PSD-95 family MAGUKs contain three PDZ domains that are known to directly interact with N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor C-termini (Kornau et al., 1995)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: PSD-95 family MAGUKs directly interact with AMPA receptor C-termini.
source: α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid (AMPA) receptor C-termini (Leonard et al., 1998)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: PSD-95 family MAGUKs directly interact with AMPA receptor auxiliary subunit C-termini.
source: and AMPA receptor auxiliary subunit C-termini (Dakoji et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The MAGUK SH3 domain lost its function to bind proline-rich peptides and instead forms an intramolecular interaction with the GK domain.
source: The MAGUK SH3 domain lost its function to bind proline-rich peptides; instead it forms an intramolecular interaction with the GK domain (McGee et al., 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The PSD-95 GK domain is unable to phosphorylate GMP but has evolved as a protein interaction domain.
source: Similarly, the PSD-95 GK domain is atypical in that it is unable to phosphorylate GMP but has evolved as a protein interaction domain (Johnston et al., 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Binding of known interactors to the GK domain typically involves residues of the canonical GMP-binding region.
source: Binding of known interactors to the GK domain typically involves residues of the canonical GMP-binding region (Reese et al., 2007; Zhu et al., 2011; Zhu et al., 2016b).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: PSD-95 family MAGUKs are essential for the establishment of long-term potentiation (LTP) by regulating the content of AMPA receptors at dendritic spines.
source: Accordingly, PSD-95 family MAGUKs are essential for the establishment of long-term potentiation (LTP) by regulating the content of AMPA receptors at dendritic spines (Ehrlich and Malinow, 2004; Opazo et al., 2012; Sheng et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Acute knockdown of PSD-95 MAGUKs leads to a decrease in postsynaptic AMPA and NMDA receptor-mediated synaptic transmission.
source: In line with this is the observation that acute knockdown of PSD-95 MAGUKs leads to a decrease in postsynaptic AMPA and NMDA receptor-mediated synaptic transmission as well as a reduction in PSD size (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Acute knockdown of PSD-95 MAGUKs leads to a reduction in PSD size.
source: In line with this is the observation that acute knockdown of PSD-95 MAGUKs leads to a decrease in postsynaptic AMPA and NMDA receptor-mediated synaptic transmission as well as a reduction in PSD size (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: PSD-95 oligomerises upon binding of monomeric CRIPT-derived PDZ3 ligands.
source: We have previously shown that the synaptic MAGUK protein PSD-95 oligomerises upon binding of monomeric CRIPT-derived PDZ3 ligands (ligands that specifically bind to the third PDZ domain) (Rademacher et al., 2013)
evidence: This is a previous finding by the authors supported by a citation to their prior work.

claim: Ligand-PDZ3 domain binding induces conformational changes in the C-terminal domains that lead to complex formation.
source: and speculated that ligand - PDZ3 domain binding induces conformational changes in the C-terminal domains that lead to complex formation.
evidence: This is a speculation based on previous observations.

claim: PDZ ligand-induced effects in PSD-95 MAGUK proteins have been supported by other studies.
source: Our initial observations of PDZ ligand-induced effects in PSD-95 MAGUK proteins have recently been supported by other studies (Zeng et al., 2016; Zeng et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to other studies.

claim: PSD-95 oligomerisation can be triggered by Neuroligin-1 (NLGN1).
source: In this study, we use a bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC) assay to show that PSD-95 oligomerisation can be triggered by Neuroligin-1 (NLGN1)
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by BiFC assay data in Figure 1.

claim: PSD-95 oligomerisation triggered by NLGN1 is dependent on the C-terminal SH3-GK domain tandem.
source: and that this is dependent on the C-terminal SH3-GK domain tandem.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by BiFC assay data in Figure 1D.

claim: Neuroligin-1 is a synaptic adhesion molecule that specifically binds to the third PDZ domain of PSD-95.
source: NLGN1 is a synaptic adhesion molecule that specifically binds to the third PDZ domain of PSD-95 (Irie et al., 1997).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Coexpression of PSD-95-YN and PSD-95-YC constructs with full-length NLGN1 led to the formation of multimolecular fluorescent PSD-95 complexes located at the cell membrane.
source: Coexpression of the per se non-fluorescent PSD-95-YN and PSD-95-YC constructs (together referred to as WT/WTsplitEYFP) with full-length NLGN1 led to the formation of multimolecular fluorescent PSD-95 complexes that were located at the cell membrane, recapitulating the natural localisation of the endogenous protein complexes (Figure 1B)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In PSD-95 complexes formed with NLGN1, the PSD-95 C-termini are in close proximity to each other.
source: and highlighting that the PSD-95 C-termini (which harbour the splitEYFP tags) are in close proximity to each other in these complexes.
evidence: This is inferred from the BiFC assay results where splitEYFP refolding indicates proximity.

claim: SynCAM1 does not bind to PSD-95 PDZ domains.
source: Fluorescence is almost not detectable by coexpression of SynCAM1 (SynCAM1 is not binding to PSD-95 PDZ domains)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figure 1C and established knowledge about SynCAM1 binding specificity.

claim: SynCAMs bind exclusively to class II PDZ domains rather than class I PDZ domains.
source: SynCAMs, like NLGNs, are trans-synaptic membrane proteins; however, they differ from NLGN family members at the C-terminus and bind exclusively to class II PDZ domains (e.g. CASK, MPP2) rather than class I PDZ domains (such as PSD-95 PDZ domains) (Biederer et al., 2002).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Mutation of the PDZ-binding sequence of NLGN1 (TTRV to TARA) decreases fluorescence intensity by approximately 40% relative to wild-type NLGN1.
source: Upon coexpression of this mutNLGN1 with splitEYFP-tagged PSD-95 molecules, the detected fluorescence intensity decreased by approximately 40% relative to that after coexpression with wild-type NLGN1 (Figure 1D, see also Figure 1—figure supplement 1 for gating strategy)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The L460P mutation in the PSD-95 SH3 domain specifically disrupts the intramolecular SH3-GK domain interaction.
source: Leucine 460 is an internal SH3 domain residue and the L460P mutation has been shown to specifically disrupt the intramolecular SH3-GK domain interaction (Figure 1—figure supplement 2) (McGee and Bredt, 1999; Shin et al., 2000)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations and validated by experimental data in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The L460P mutation strongly abolishes PSD-95 complex assembly as observed by EYFP refolding.
source: Interestingly, this amino acid exchange does not interfere with PDZ3 ligand binding (Rademacher et al., 2013) but strongly abolishes PSD-95 complex assembly, as observed by EYFP refolding (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The L460P mutation does not interfere with PDZ3 ligand binding.
source: Interestingly, this amino acid exchange does not interfere with PDZ3 ligand binding (Rademacher et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The intramolecular SH3-GK domain interaction is a hallmark feature of MAGUK proteins.
source: that is one of the hallmark features of MAGUK proteins (Tavares et al., 2001).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The L460P mutation results in a constitutively 'open' conformation of the SH3-GK domain tandem.
source: We assume that in the context of the full-length protein, the L460P mutation likewise weakens the (intramolecular) interaction between the SH3 and GK domains, which would then result in a constitutively 'open' conformation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known effects of the L460P mutation.

claim: PSD-95 constructs efficiently oligomerise and coprecipitate upon binding of a PDZ3 ligand.
source: In line with our BiFC assay results, we have previously reported that PSD-95 constructs (full-length and the isolated PSG module) efficiently oligomerise and coprecipitate upon binding of a PDZ3 ligand (Rademacher et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a previous finding by the authors supported by a citation.

claim: The PSG module forms a dynamic modular entity.
source: Moreover, the observation by NMR spectroscopy that the PSG module forms a dynamic modular entity (Zhang et al., 2013)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: CRIPT is a cytosolic protein that interacts predominantly with the third PDZ domain of PSD-95.
source: For these experiments, we again took advantage of the PSD-95 interactor CRIPT, which is a cytosolic protein that has been shown to interact predominantly with the third PDZ domain of PSD-95 (Niethammer et al., 1998).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The CRIPT-derived mutPDZ3 ligand (DTKNYKQASA) almost completely abrogates binding to PDZ3.
source: As a control, comparable constructs carrying two amino acid exchanges within the PDZ3 ligand sequence (DTKNYKQASA) were used. In our hands, this mutation in the CRIPT C-terminus almost completely abrogates binding to PDZ3, as observed by coIP (Rademacher et al., 2013)
evidence: This is supported by a citation to previous work.

claim: The SH3-GK construct did not coprecipitate with the PSG module regardless of whether it was coexpressed with wild-type or mutant CRIPT-derived PDZ3 ligands.
source: The SH3-GK construct did not coprecipitate with the PSG module regardless of whether it was coexpressed with wild-type or mutant CRIPT-derived PDZ3 ligands.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The GK domain alone coprecipitated effectively with the PSG module when expressed in the presence of functional CRIPT-derived PDZ3 ligands.
source: The GK domain alone, however, coprecipitated effectively with the PSG module, when expressed in the presence of functional CRIPT-derived PDZ3 ligands.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Binding of a CRIPT-derived PDZ3 ligand renders the PSG module 'interaction-competent' to bind isolated GK domain constructs in trans.
source: These data suggest that binding of a CRIPT-derived PDZ3 ligand renders the PSG module 'interaction-competent'; that is it facilitates formation of a conformational state in which it is able to bind isolated GK domain constructs in trans.
evidence: This is an inference based on the coimmunoprecipitation data in Figure 1E.

claim: The intramolecular SH3-GK domain assembly resembles the 'interaction-incompetent' state where the SH3 domain autoinhibits the GK domain's interaction activity.
source: In this experiment, the intramolecular SH3-GK domain assembly resembles the 'interaction-incompetent' state, and the SH3 domain autoinhibits the GK domain's interaction activity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental results.

claim: 278 proteins were reproducibly identified and quantified in the mass spectrometry experiment.
source: In total, we reproducibly identified and quantified 278 proteins (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by the mass spectrometry data.

claim: Approximately 82% of the identified proteins have been reported to be present in mouse and/or human cortical postsynaptic density fractions.
source: Remarkably, 230 (≈ 82%) of these have been reported to be present in mouse and/or human cortical postsynaptic density fractions (Bayés et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by comparison with published data cited.

claim: Map1A is a known GK-domain interacting protein.
source: Moreover, we also identified the known GK-domain interacting proteins Map1A (Reese et al., 2007)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation and validated by the mass spectrometry data.

claim: Mark2 is a known GK-domain interacting protein.
source: Mark2 (Wu et al., 2012)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation and validated by the mass spectrometry data.

claim: Dlgap2 is a known GK-domain interacting protein.
source: Dlgap2 (Takeuchi et al., 1997)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation and validated by the mass spectrometry data.

claim: Srcin1/p140CAP is a known GK-domain interacting protein.
source: and Srcin1/p140CAP (Fossati et al., 2015)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation and validated by the mass spectrometry data.

claim: Several heterotrimeric G protein subunits were enriched in the protein fractions that bind preferentially to the GST-GK construct.
source: Unexpectedly, we isolated several heterotrimeric G protein subunits enriched in the protein fractions that bind preferentially to the GST-GK construct (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by the mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Gnb5 is a signalling effector downstream of GPCRs that exhibits inhibitory activity in neurons.
source: Of special interest was the guanine nucleotide binding protein beta 5 (Gnb5), which is a signalling effector downstream of GPCRs that exhibits inhibitory activity in neurons (Xie et al., 2010; Ostrovskaya et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Gnb5 contains an N-terminal α-helix followed by a β-sheet propeller composed of seven WD-40 repeats.
source: Gnb5 contains an N-terminal α-helix followed by a β-sheet propeller composed of seven WD-40 repeats (Cheever et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Gnb5 is specifically expressed in brain.
source: Gnb5 is specifically expressed in brain (Watson et al., 1994)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Mutations in the Gnb5 gene cause a multisystem syndrome with intellectual disability in patients.
source: and mutations in the Gnb5 gene cause a multisystem syndrome with intellectual disability in patients (Lodder et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Gnb5 was not detected in the bead control pull-down.
source: We could not detect Gnb5 in the bead control pull-down lane
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Almost no Gnb5 was detectable in the GST-SH3-GK lane.
source: and almost no Gnb5 was detectable in the GST-SH3-GK lane.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: A clear Gnb5 signal was present in the GST-GK lane.
source: However, a clear Gnb5 signal was present in the GST-GK lane
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: A Gnb5-GK domain interaction is favoured over a Gnb5-SH3-GK domain interaction.
source: supporting our quantitative mass spectrometry results and suggesting that a Gnb5 - GK domain interaction is favoured over a Gnb5 - SH3-GK domain interaction.
evidence: This is an inference based on the GST pull-down data in Figure 3A.

claim: Overexpressed Gnb5 preferentially interacts with the isolated GK domain compared to SH3-GK domain constructs in COS-7 cells.
source: Additionally, we observed a preferred interaction of overexpressed Gnb5 with the isolated GK domain compared to SH3-GK domain constructs in COS-7 cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Upon IP of Gnb5-Clover, the isolated GK domain coprecipitates far more efficiently than the SH3-GK domain.
source: Upon IP of Gnb5 tagged with the green fluorescent protein Clover (Lam et al., 2012) using αGFP antibodies, the isolated GK domain coprecipitates far more efficiently than does the SH3-GK domain (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Gnb5 staining is present in neuronal dendrites where the signal overlaps with PSD-95 staining.
source: Gnb5 staining was present in neuronal dendrites, where the signal overlaps with the PSD-95 staining (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The Gnb5 signal is adjacent to the presynaptic Synapsin signal.
source: In these experiments, the Gnb5 signal is adjacent to the presynaptic Synapsin signal (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The presence of CRIPT-derived PDZ3 ligands triggers coimmunoprecipitation of Gnb5 and PSD-95.
source: Following IP of PSD-95, the precipitates were analysed by western blot: the presence of these PDZ3 ligands indeed triggered coimmunoprecipitation of Gnb5 and PSD-95
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Gnb5 lacking the N-terminal α-helix (shortGnb5) coprecipitated somewhat less efficiently than the full-length protein.
source: Gnb5 lacking the N-terminal α-helix (shortGnb5) coprecipitated somewhat less efficiently than the full-length protein (Figure 4A)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The N-terminal region of Gnb5 (amino acids 1–33) is important for the PDZ3 ligand-mediated interaction with PSD-95.
source: suggesting that this N-terminal region of Gnb5 (amino acids 1–33) is important for the PDZ3 ligand-mediated interaction with PSD-95.
evidence: This is an inference based on the coimmunoprecipitation data in Figure 4A.

claim: The PSG module is sufficient for ligand-triggered coimmunoprecipitation of Gnb5.
source: Clearly, the PSG module is sufficient for ligand-triggered coimmunoprecipitation of Gnb5.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Gnb5 did not coprecipitate efficiently with the wild-type PSG module.
source: Gnb5 did not coprecipitate efficiently with the wild-type PSG module
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Gnb5 was effectively coprecipitated by the PSG module harbouring the L460P mutation.
source: but was effectively coprecipitated by the PSG module harbouring the L460P mutation that disrupts the intramolecular SH3-GK domain interaction (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Various PSD-95 GK-interacting proteins bind to the canonical GMP-binding region.
source: Interestingly, various PSD-95 GK-interacting proteins bind to the canonical GMP-binding region, and by exchanging arginine 568 (which is situated in the ancestral GMP-binding site) to alanine (R568A), these interactions can be specifically disrupted (Reese et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: GKAP is an established synaptic GK domain binder.
source: GKAP ('GK'-associated protein, also referred to as SAPAP1 or DLGAP1) is an established synaptic GK domain binder (Kim et al., 1997)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: GKAP interaction with PSD-95 involves the GMP-binding region.
source: whose interaction involves the GMP-binding region (Zhu et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: GKAP can be efficiently coprecipitated upon pull-down of either the isolated GK domain or an intact PSG module.
source: These ideas are also validated by our own coimmunoprecipitation experiments: GKAP can be efficiently coprecipitated upon pull-down of either the isolated GK domain or an intact PSG module
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: A recombinant PSG module harbouring the GMP binding site mutation R568A fails to precipitate GKAP.
source: whereas a recombinant PSG module harbouring the GMP binding site mutation R568A fails to precipitate GKAP (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The R568A mutation had no effect on coprecipitation of Gnb5 with PSD-95.
source: In experiments with PSD-95 and Gnb5, however, the same mutation had no effect on coprecipitation of Gnb5 (Figure 5B)
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: GKAP and Gnb5 proteins bind to PSD-95 GK domains in fundamentally different ways.
source: suggesting that GKAP and Gnb5 proteins bind to PSD-95 GK domains in fundamentally different ways.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential effects of the R568A mutation on GKAP and Gnb5 binding.

claim: The presence of PDZ3 ligands did not substantially influence the GKAP-PSD-95 interaction.
source: The presence of PDZ3 ligands did not substantially influence the GKAP interaction: PSD-95 binds GKAP regardless of whether wild-type or mutant CRIPT-derived PDZ3 ligands were present (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Ligand binding to PDZ3 results in a conformational change of the intramolecular SH3-GK interaction.
source: Importantly, our data support a model in which ligand binding to PDZ3 results in a conformational change of the 'resting' intramolecular SH3-GK interaction that is common to MAGUK proteins.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: In the resting state, the external GK surface harbouring the classical GMP binding site is available for protein-protein interaction with GKAP and MAP1a.
source: In the resting state, the external GK surface harbouring the classical GMP binding site is available for protein-protein interaction such as those with the well-known PSD-95 interactors GKAP and MAP1a.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data and established knowledge.

claim: Upon ligand binding, GK surfaces other than the GMP binding site become accessible for protein-protein interactions.
source: However, upon ligand binding, other GK surfaces become accessible for protein-protein interactions.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data.

claim: Gnb5 binds to GK domain surfaces that differ from the GMP-binding site.
source: A subset of synaptic GK-interacting proteins – in particular Gnb5, and perhaps other proteins enriched in our pool of interacting proteins that bind preferentially to GK rather than to SH3-GK – bind to these surfaces of the GK domain (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing differential binding patterns.

claim: The molecular basis for the dynamic regulation of synaptic transmission is dependent on the assembly and disassembly of protein complexes.
source: The molecular basis for the dynamic regulation of synaptic transmission is dependent on the assembly and disassembly of protein complexes (Yokoi et al., 2012; Lautz et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Activity-dependent changes in synaptic protein networks depend on phosphorylation.
source: It is also well established that activity-dependent changes in synaptic protein networks depend on phosphorylation (Opazo et al., 2010; Araki et al., 2015; Li et al., 2016)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Activity-dependent changes in synaptic protein networks depend on palmitoylation.
source: and other post-translational modifications, such as palmitoylation (El-Husseini et al., 2002; Fukata et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The minimal requirement for the amplification of synaptic signals is the interaction of glutamate receptor auxiliary subunits with postsynaptic scaffold proteins.
source: Recently, it has been reported that the minimal requirement for the amplification of synaptic signals is the interaction of glutamate receptor auxiliary subunits with postsynaptic scaffold proteins; specifically the interaction between different PDZ ligand C-termini and synaptic MAGUKs can trigger a common molecular mechanism necessary for the induction of long-term potentiation downstream of glutamate receptors (Sheng et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: PSD-95 plays a central role in activity-dependent synapse regulation.
source: In this study, we focussed on the postsynaptic scaffold protein PSD-95, which plays a central role in activity-dependent synapse regulation (Ehrlich et al., 2007).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Protein complex formation guided by PSD-95 PDZ and GK domains can be reversibly regulated by phosphorylation.
source: It is established that protein complex formation guided by PSD-95 PDZ and GK domains can be reversibly regulated by phosphorylation (Sumioka et al., 2010; Zhu et al., 2017)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: At postsynaptic membranes, various PDZ ligand C-termini of multimeric receptor complexes are available to form multivalent interactions with scaffold proteins.
source: and at postsynaptic membranes, various PDZ ligand C-termini of multimeric receptor complexes are available to form multivalent interactions with scaffold proteins (Schwenk et al., 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Binding of a SynGAP-derived PDZ ligand peptide was sufficient to induce PSD-95 PSG construct dimerisation.
source: More recently, it was shown by others that binding of a SynGAP-derived PDZ ligand peptide was sufficient to induce PSD-95 PSG construct dimerisation (Zeng et al., 2016)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: SynGAP-induced conformational coupling between the PDZ3 domain and the SH3-GK module plays a role in PSD-95 dimerisation.
source: and the same group subsequently explored how SynGAP-induced conformational coupling between the PDZ3 domain and the SH3-GK module plays a role in this process (Zeng et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Gnb5 acts in a heterodimeric complex together with RGS7 to functionally couple GIRK channels to GABAB receptors.
source: Gnb5 acts in a heterodimeric complex together with RGS7 to functionally couple GIRK channels to GABAB receptors (Xie et al., 2010; Ostrovskaya et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Upon activation of GABAB receptors, the Gnb5-RGS7 complex promotes fast deactivation of GIRK channels.
source: Upon activation of GABAB receptors, the Gnb5-RGS7 complex promotes fast deactivation of GIRK channels (Fajardo-Serrano et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The interaction between RGS proteins and Gnb5 involves the N-terminal helical domain of Gnb5 and the G protein gamma-subunit-like (GGL) domain of RGS proteins.
source: Interestingly, the interaction between RGS proteins and Gnb5 involves the N-terminal helical domain of Gnb5 and the G protein gamma-subunit-like (GGL) domain of RGS proteins (Cheever et al., 2008).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: PSD-95 SH3 and GK domains, when expressed independently, bind each other efficiently.
source: Indeed, PSD-95 SH3 and GK domains, when expressed independently, bind each other efficiently (McGee and Bredt, 1999; Shin et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Mutations that disrupt the interface where SH3 and GK domains contact each other can have detrimental effects on protein function.
source: Likewise, in line with this structural model, mutations that disrupt the interface where these two domains contact each other can have detrimental effects on protein function (McGee and Bredt, 1999; Shin et al., 2000).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: The SH3 domain has been reported to be an allosteric regulator or inhibitor of GK domain binding function.
source: Also relevant is the fact that the SH3 domain has been reported to be an allosteric regulator or inhibitor of GK domain binding function, not only by direct contact with the adjacent GK surface but also by regulating the conformation of distant GK domain surfaces (Marcette et al., 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Binding of a ligand to the PSD-95 PDZ3 domain may influence the allosteric regulatory function of the neighbouring SH3 domain.
source: It is possible that binding of a ligand to the PSD-95 PDZ3 domain influences precisely this function of the neighbouring SH3 domain and thus indirectly regulates GK interactions at distant sites.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the experimental observations.

claim: Regulation via PDZ3 ligand binding may result in a conformational change that loosens the natural SH3-GK structure, thereby freeing up the SH3-interacting surface of the GK domain for other protein-protein interactions.
source: Alternatively, it is conceivable that regulation via PDZ3 ligand binding results in a conformational change that loosens the natural SH3-GK structure, thereby freeing up the SH3-interacting surface of the GK domain for other protein-protein interactions.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the experimental observations.

claim: The canonical GMP-binding region in the GK domain is not allosterically regulated by PDZ3 ligand binding.
source: This result suggests that the canonical GMP-binding region in the GK domain is not allosterically regulated by PDZ3 ligand binding.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that GKAP binding is not influenced by PDZ3 ligand binding.

claim: Gnb5 might occupy a different GK domain surface for interaction that does not directly overlap with the canonical GMP-binding site.
source: First of all, the R568A mutation had no effect on the Gnb5 - PSD-95 interaction, suggesting that Gnb5 might occupy a different GK domain surface for interaction – one that does not directly overlap with the canonical GMP-binding site responsible for the GKAP interaction.
evidence: This is an inference based on the differential effects of the R568A mutation.

claim: The SH3 domain exerts inhibitory activity on the GK domain binding capacity by competing directly with Gnb5 for interaction surfaces.
source: We propose that the Gnb5 - PSD-95 interaction is regulated by a modular allosteric mechanism: the SH3 domain exerts inhibitory activity on the GK domain binding capacity by competing directly with Gnb5 for interaction surfaces.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental data.

claim: The PSD-95 SH3-GK domain tandem undergoes structural rearrangements upon binding of a CRIPT-derived PDZ3 ligand to the adjacent PDZ3 domain.
source: Our data are in line with a model in which the PSD-95 SH3-GK domain tandem undergoes structural rearrangements upon binding of a CRIPT-derived PDZ3 ligand to the adjacent PDZ3 domain, and these changes free up the GK domain for interactions with selected proteins.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental data.

claim: SynGAP specifically influences conformational coupling between PDZ3 and the SH3-GK module in PSD-95, while the related SAP102 does not undergo the same mechanistic alterations.
source: Data from other groups suggest that SynGAP, which also binds to PSD-95 PDZ3, specifically influences conformational coupling between PDZ3 and the SH3-GK module, while the related SAP102 does not undergo the same mechanistic alterations (Zeng et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Kinase-mediated signalling in response to changes in synaptic activity can influence binding affinity of ligands for PDZ3 domains.
source: Moreover, kinase-mediated signalling in response to changes in synaptic activity can also influence binding affinity of ligands for PDZ3 domains (Walkup et al., 2016)
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Coexpression of PSD-95-YN, PSD-95-YC and full-length Neuroligin-1 reveals a membrane associated localisation of the refolded complex.
source: Live-cell microscopy of HEK-293T cells transfected with PSD-95-YN, PSD-95-YC and full-length Neuroligin-1 reveals a membrane associated localisation of the refolded complex (transfection corresponding to WT/WTsplitEYFP plus NLGN1 in Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by the microscopy image in Figure 1B.

claim: Formation of oligomeric fluorescent complexes is effective in the presence of wild-type Neuroligin-1.
